findings.title: Updates made while the owning org is disabled skip login-cache invalidation
findings.description:
`update()` (line 91) loads `original` through `getById`, which returns the org-aware wrapper from `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (lines 432-446). That wrapper's `isEnabled()` is false whenever the owning org is disabled. `updated` is the raw model. So for an org-bound IdP whose org is disabled, `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is always false.

Trigger sequence:
1. Org O is enabled. IdP X (org O, enabled, BROKER_PUBLIC=true, not hidden) is cached in the ORG_ONLY and ALL lists.
2. Disable O. `OrganizationAdapter.setEnabled` only calls `registerOrganizationInvalidation`, which touches the org and org-IdP-list keys (`InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:300-315`). No login key is invalidated.
3. Set X's `hideOnLogin=true`, or remove `BROKER_PUBLIC`. Both sides of the check evaluate false, so the early return at lines 405-407 skips invalidation.
4. Re-enable O. Still no login invalidation.

The cached list still contains X. On the anonymous login page, `IdentityProviderBean.getProviders()` (lines 73-77) calls `searchForIdentityProviders`, which does not apply `federatedProviderPredicate()`. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75` and `:80` only re-check `isEnabled()`. X is therefore rendered even though it is hidden, or even though it is no longer public, which can expose a non-public org IdP on the general login page.

The Javadoc at lines 391-402 promises invalidation "in all other scenarios", and this path violates that. Suggested fix: evaluate `original` against the raw stored model rather than the org-aware wrapper, or conservatively invalidate when either side has an `organizationId` and the raw predicate result changed. Add a test for disable → hide/unpublish → re-enable → assert the login list excludes the IdP.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers the literal alias "alias", so the IdPs are never removed
findings.description: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` removes an IdP named `"alias"`, which does not exist. The same mistake is at line 425, which covers `idp-alias-20`. `TestCleanup.addCleanup` swallows every exception (`testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/util/TestCleanup.java:65-72`), so none of the 21 IdPs created by the test are removed, and they leak into the shared realm. The pattern is copied from pre-existing line 303, outside this diff. Suggested fix: use the real aliases, or the existing `TestCleanup.addIdentityProviderAlias(alias)`.

findings.title: Coverage gaps in the invalidation matrix
findings.description:
The test covers create/remove of non-login IdPs, updates that keep login status, and linking. It does not cover:
- Org disable/enable combined with IdP edits. This is exactly where the FAIL above sits.
- Unlinking a login-eligible public org IdP via `removeIdentityProvider` (`JpaOrganizationProvider.java:358-374`).
- Removing an org-linked login IdP.
- The `isEnabled()` re-check added to `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, which has no test in this diff.

The single ~170-line method also repeats the "check all caches" loop five times. A helper would make the matrix easier to extend. At minimum, add the org-disable and unlink cases.

findings.title: `getForLogin` duplicates `getByOrganization`, and the invalidation loop is duplicated
findings.description: The new `getForLogin` (lines 214-255) is a near line-for-line copy of `getByOrganization` (lines 167-211). Both contain the same invalidation check, the same query/revision/`invalidateObject` state machine, and the same ID→`getById` fallback. The loop `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values()) realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(...))` also appears at lines 385-387 and 415-417. Any fix to the state machine, including the one needed for the FAIL, must now be made in two places. Suggested fix: extract a shared helper parameterized by cache key and fetch function, and a single `registerLoginInvalidation()` helper.

findings.title: `remove()` now always performs an uncached DB lookup
findings.description: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` moved above the `isInvalid` branch, so every IdP removal now runs a DB read. Before this change it ran only on the invalidated path. The impact is small because admin deletes are rare. The cached branch at line 105 already holds a `CachedIdentityProvider` that could supply the state the login predicate needs.

findings.title: Public SPI docs do not describe the new login rule
findings.description: `getLoginPredicate()` now requires `BROKER_PUBLIC` for org-bound IdPs (line 254). It is also the predicate behind `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` (`services/.../IdentityProviderBean.java:226`), so the base bean's linked-identity list changes too. The `getForLogin` Javadoc (lines 151-153) and the `LoginFilter` Javadoc (lines 215-217) still describe eligibility as enabled / not link-only / not hidden. `getLoginPredicate()` has no Javadoc at all. Update the docs, and note the behavior change for implementors of custom providers and beans.

findings.title: `removeAll()` invalidates the count key but not the login keys
findings.description: `removeAll()` calls `registerCountInvalidation()` but not the login-key invalidation. The only caller is realm removal (`model/jpa/.../JpaRealmProvider.java:207`). Realm IDs are normally unique, so the impact is low. Still, every other IdP mutation in this diff invalidates the login keys. Adding `registerLoginInvalidation()` here is cheap.

findings.title: Create, remove, and link/unlink invalidation are correct for the non-org-disabled case
findings.description:
I traced these paths:
- `create()` and `remove()` evaluate the raw model (`remove()` uses the DB-loaded `storedIdp`), so the org-disabled wrapper does not affect them.
- `JpaOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider` and `removeIdentityProvider` route through `session.identityProviders().update(...)` (`JpaOrganizationProvider.java:341-342` and `:368-371`), so link/unlink reaches the invalidation logic.

I also checked the expected counts in `testCacheIDPForLogin` (REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL = 5/5/10, then 6/5/11, then 5/6/11). They hold given the fixture: the `@Before` org brokers are not `BROKER_PUBLIC` (no broker delegate in the base test tree sets it), so they are excluded from the public-only queries. The counts are not verified by execution.
